blocks.explanation:
Yeh G.M. (geometric mean, yani hindsi ausat) ki definition ka seedha istemal hai. \(G\) us waqt \(a\) aur \(b\) ka G.M. hota hai jab \(a, G, b\) G.P. mein hon.
Diya kya hai? \(a = -2\) aur \(b = 8\). Find kya karna hai? \(G\).
Plan: \(G^{2} = ab\) lagayenge, phir \(\pm\) ke saath square root lenge. Dhyan rahe ke product negative aayega, is liye jawab mein \(i\) aayega.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a = -2\), \(b = 8\).
Humein find karna hai: G.M. \(G\).
Tareeqa: Agar \(a, G, b\) G.P. mein hain to har term ko pichle term se divide karne par ek hi ratio aata hai: \(\frac{G}{a} = \frac{b}{G}\). Cross multiply karein to \(G^{2} = ab\), yani \(G = \pm\sqrt{ab}\). Yahi formula is sawal ke liye fit hai kyunke humein sirf do numbers ke beech ek G.M. chahiye.

Dono numbers ko multiply karein
\[ab = (-2)(8)\]
\[= -16\]
Kyun: Formula kehta hai ke \(G^{2}\) product ke barabar hai, is liye pehle product nikalte hain. Minus ko plus se multiply karein to minus hi aata hai.
Dhyan dein: Yahan A.M. wala formula \(\frac{a+b}{2}\) nahi lagana; woh jama (addition) wala ausat hai, G.M. zarb (multiplication) wala ausat hai.

Square root lein
\[G = \pm\sqrt{-16}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{16}\,\sqrt{-1}\]
\[= \pm 4i\]
Kyun: \(-16\) ko \(16 \times (-1)\) likh sakte hain. \(\sqrt{16} = 4\) aur Unit 1 se humein maloom hai ke \(\sqrt{-1} = i\) (iota). Kisi negative number ka real square root nahi hota, is liye yahan dono G.M. imaginary hain. \(\pm\) is liye ke \(4i\) aur \(-4i\) dono ka square \(-16\) hai.

Tasdeeq: \(G^{2}\) ko \(-16\) aana chahiye
\[(\pm 4i)^{2} = 16i^{2} = -16\]
Kyun: \(i^{2} = -1\), is liye \(16i^{2} = -16\). Ratio se bhi dekh lein: \(-2, 4i, 8\) mein \(\frac{4i}{-2} = -2i\) aur \(\frac{8}{4i} = \frac{2}{i} = -2i\). Dono ratios barabar hain, yani yeh waqai G.P. hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh bilkul (i) jaisa sawal hai, farq sirf itna hai ke ab dono numbers mein \(i\) hai.
Find kya karna hai? \(G\), jahan \(G^{2} = ab\).
Plan: \((-2i)(8i)\) ko dhyan se multiply karenge aur \(i^{2} = -1\) lagayenge, phir \(\pm\) ke saath square root lenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a = -2i\), \(b = 8i\).
Humein find karna hai: G.M. \(G\).
Tareeqa: Wohi formula \(G^{2} = ab\), yani \(G = \pm\sqrt{ab}\). Formula complex numbers ke liye bhi wesa hi kaam karta hai, kyunke G.P. ki shart (ratio barabar ho) wohi hai.

Dono numbers ko multiply karein
\[ab = (-2i)(8i)\]
\[= -16i^{2}\]
\[= -16(-1) = 16\]
Kyun: Number wale hisse alag multiply karein (\(-2 \times 8 = -16\)) aur \(i\) wale alag (\(i \times i = i^{2}\)). Phir \(i^{2} = -1\) rakhein; minus into minus plus ban jata hai, is liye product \(16\) aaya.
Dhyan dein: Bohat se students \(i^{2}\) ko \(-1\) karna bhool jate hain aur \(-16\) likh dete hain; phir jawab \(\pm 4i\) aa jata hai jo ghalat hai.

Square root lein
\[G = \pm\sqrt{16} = \pm 4\]
Kyun: Product ab positive real number hai, is liye square root bhi real hai. Dilchasp baat yeh hai ke dono numbers imaginary the lekin un ka G.M. real nikla.

Tasdeeq: \(G^{2}\) ko \(16\) aana chahiye
\[(\pm 4)^{2} = 16\]
Kyun: Ratio se bhi check karein: \(\frac{4}{-2i} = \frac{-2}{i} = 2i\) aur \(\frac{8i}{4} = 2i\). Ratio barabar hai, is liye \(-2i, 4, 8i\) G.P. hai aur humara jawab sahi hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is dafa dono numbers positive hain, is liye G.M. real aayenge.
Find kya karna hai? \(G = \pm\sqrt{ab}\).
Plan: pehle multiply karenge, phir \(\sqrt{54}\) ko surd (jazr wali shakal) mein simplify karenge, yani sab se bara perfect square bahar nikalenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a = 6\), \(b = 9\).
Humein find karna hai: G.M. \(G\).
Tareeqa: \(G^{2} = ab\), is liye \(G = \pm\sqrt{ab}\).

Dono numbers ko multiply karein
\[ab = 6 \times 9 = 54\]
Kyun: G.M. ka square hamesha dono numbers ke product ke barabar hota hai, is liye pehla kaam product nikalna hai.

Square root lein aur simplify karein
\[G = \pm\sqrt{54}\]
\[= \pm\sqrt{9 \times 6}\]
\[= \pm 3\sqrt{6}\]
Kyun: \(54\) perfect square nahi hai, lekin us ke andar \(9\) ek perfect square factor hai: \(54 = 9 \times 6\). \(\sqrt{9} = 3\) bahar aa jata hai aur \(\sqrt{6}\) andar reh jata hai.
Dhyan dein: \(54 = 2 \times 27\) likh kar ruk na jayein; hamesha sab se bara perfect square (yahan 9) dhoondein.

Tasdeeq: \(G^{2}\) ko \(54\) aana chahiye
\[(3\sqrt{6})^{2} = 9 \times 6 = 54\]
Kyun: Square karne se root khatam ho jata hai aur wapas product mil jata hai. Andaza bhi laga lein: \(3\sqrt{6} \approx 7.35\), jo 6 aur 9 ke darmiyan hai; positive G.P. ka beech wala term isi tarah dono ke darmiyan hota hai.
